title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred): k = F_q with q = p^f, W = W(k), and A a p-adic base, apparently a complete DVR with uniformizer π that contains W, or at least has residue field containing k. The goal is to classify semilinear-algebra data of Dieudonné/crystal type on A carrying an extra action of W.

(1) A⊗_{Z_p}W is étale over A. Since k⊗_{F_p}k ≅ k^Σ, with Σ = Aut k = Aut W ≅ Z/fZ, one gets A⊗_{Z_p}W ≅ A^Σ = ∏_{ν∈Σ} A. Here Σ is identified with [0,f−1] by ν ↦ σ^ν.

(2) The Frobenius σ_A on A⊗W (namely 1⊗σ) becomes, on A^Σ, the cyclic shift (x_0,…,x_{f−1}) ↦ (x_1,…,x_{f−1},x_0).

(3) Consequently a module M over A⊗W is the same as a family (M_ν)_{ν∈Σ} of A-modules (eigencomponents for the W-action), and rk_A M = Σ rk M_ν, wanted equal to h. A σ_A-linear endomorphism F_M is the same as a cycle of A-linear maps M_0 →φ_0 M_1 →φ_1 … → M_{f−1} →φ_{f−1} M_0.

(4) The condition (*), presumably that F_M is an isogeny (or that F_M^f, resp. V F, is π^e times an isomorphism), implies the f circular composites are isogenies. Hence each φ_i is injective, the ranks of the M_ν are all equal, and each φ_i is an isogeny. With Σ rk = h (and h = f), each M_ν is invertible.

(5) Normalization. Fix M_0 = Ω (an invertible A-module). Identify M_0 ≅ M_ν via π^{−m_ν}(φ_{ν−1}…φ_0), where 0 = m_0 ≤ m_1 ≤ … ≤ m_{f−1} are the π-adic valuations of the partial composites. Then M ≅ Ω⊗_{Z_p}W = Ω⊗_A(A⊗W), and F is determined by the exponents m_ν (and a unit). Grothendieck calls this 'un beau cas'.

This is the Dieudonné-module/crystal side of p-divisible groups of height f with formal multiplication by W(F_{p^f}), i.e. Lubin–Tate-type or 'strict W-module' objects. It is the semilinear-algebra analogue of Raynaud's classification of F-vector space schemes by exponents. The margin seems to say the same works for (*) with π replaced by an arbitrary element of A.
errors: A⊗_{Z_p}W ≅ A^Σ requires A (or A/p, with A henselian) to contain k. This hypothesis is not stated on the page, though it is implicit from 'k⊗k ≅ k^Σ'.
Concluding that the M_ν are invertible needs h = f (equal ranks r with fr = h). That the φ_i are injective requires M torsion-free over a domain A.

The normalization π^{−m_ν}(φ_{ν−1}…φ_0) being an isomorphism uses that A is a DVR (or that the composites are π-power multiples of isomorphisms). The marginal generalization to arbitrary π in A would need extra hypotheses.
The final M ≅ Ω⊗_{Z_p}W describes the underlying module only. The Frobenius structure is encoded by the m_ν and a unit, which the page does not record explicitly.

ideas.what: Splitting A⊗_{Z_p}W ≅ A^{Z/f}, with Frobenius acting as cyclic shift, and decomposition of σ-semilinear modules into eigencomponents with a cycle of linear maps
ideas.modern_name: Eigenspace decomposition of Dieudonné modules with W(F_q)-action (σ-cycles)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; used by Raynaud (1974), Fontaine, and in the Lubin–Tate / Drinfeld literature
ideas.where_published: Possibly implicit in 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1970/74)

ideas.what: Classification of rank-one-per-component F-modules over a DVR by nondecreasing exponents m_ν (valuations of partial composites of φ)
ideas.modern_name: Classification of Lubin–Tate / Raynaud-type F_q-module schemes and their Dieudonné modules via exponents
ideas.usually_credited_to: M. Raynaud, 'Schémas en groupes de type (p,…,p)' (1974); Lubin–Tate; Hazewinkel

missed.claim: Grothendieck, around 1970 in his crystal notes, carries out a Raynaud-style classification of Dieudonné-type modules with multiplication by W(F_{p^f}) via exponents m_ν. This predates or parallels Raynaud 1974 and is not documented as his.
missed.quote: M_0 ≅ M_ν donnés par π^{-m_ν}(φ_{ν-1}φ_{ν-2}⋯φ_0), où m_ν est un entier ≥0 convenablement déterminé … On trouve donc un beau cas.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest for attributing exponent-type classifications of Lubin–Tate-like objects. Mathematically it is routine and well known.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but standard semilinear-algebra computation (eigencomponent decomposition and exponent normalization) that is well established in later literature (Raynaud, Lubin–Tate theory). The only interest is historical, as context in Grothendieck's crystal / Barsotti–Tate work.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'On a A⊗_{Z_p}W étale sur A, et évidemment k⊗_{F_p}k ≃ k^Σ, Σ = Aut k = Aut W' looks right.
The marginal note reads roughly 'ce serait aussi vrai avec conditions (*) … avec π un élément quelconque de A' rather than 'un objet'.
'h' in '(on le veut égal à h)' refers to the total rank. 'M_0 = t' is likely 'M_0 = Ω' (an invertible module), consistent with the final formula M ≅ Ω⊗W.
